clue.text: Bread and milk supplier's nice little earner

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash
a cow supplies milk

explanation.surface: A dairy and bakery business turns out to be a nice little earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is an idiom for a reliable source of steady profit.

clue.text: "Rustle" Crowe (cringe!)

indicators.note: to rustle is to stir things about, so the letters of the name are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An aside about the actor Russell Crowe, inviting the reader to wince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustle' rearranges CROWE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back in fear, a synonym of cringe.

clue.text: Slur about Guardian Bear

indicators.note: the word for a slur goes round, about, the newspaper's self-reference

parts.note: a slur on someone's name is a stain on it
the Guardian newspaper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: The Guardian insults a bear, or insults a bear it owns.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Guardian crossword 'Guardian' can mean the paper speaking of itself, in the first person plural; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight or a loss is to sustain it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: See 23
Theologian/philosopher giving direction on version of "Oklahoma!" (filmic)

indicators.note: in a down clue the direction sits on top of what follows

parts.note: W is west, a compass direction

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so the letters of the musical and the adjective are rearranged

parts.note: the musical's name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker comments on a screen adaptation of the musical Oklahoma!
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges OKLAHOMA plus FILMIC into ILLIAMOFOCKHAM, placed under W ('on').
explanation.definitionFit: William of Ockham was a medieval English friar, theologian and philosopher, known for Ockham's razor.

clue.text: Deity misspelt as such after carriage return

indicators.note: the jumbled word comes after the turned vehicle
the vehicle's name is taken back the other way

parts.note: a cab is a horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: the word is spelt wrongly, so its letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A typing note: the god's name got misspelt after hitting carriage return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CAB into BAC; 'misspelt' turns SUCH into CHUS. 'Carriage return' looks like a typewriter key.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine, so a deity.

clue.text: He was not idealistically philosophical, Mark, accepting role initially in film by Spielberg, the controversial director

indicators.note: the mark takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a brand is a mark burned or stamped on something

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the film's title

parts.note: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial was directed by Steven Spielberg

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word role is wanted

parts.note: Ken Russell was a British film director famed for provocative films

explanation.surface: A long biographical riddle about a non-idealist who took a part in a Spielberg film by a notorious director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'accepting' nest the pieces to build the first name. Ken Russell made Women in Love and The Devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell led the British revolt against idealism in philosophy, championing realism and logical analysis.

clue.text: Colour of swan with an extremely light down

parts.note: a cob is a male swan

indicators.note: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word light are taken

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue

explanation.surface: Describing a swan whose feathers are a very pale down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like feathers but means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt blue is a deep blue pigment, so it names a colour.

clue.text: Shock! Pin-up might go to one's head

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A scandalous pin-up picture might turn one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LEG to GEL. 'Pin-up' reads as a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gel is applied to the hair, so it literally goes on one's head.

clue.text: Cover put away in "Quiet Man"

indicators.note: the eating goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
he is the pronoun for a man
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Something is concealed in the John Wayne film The Quiet Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quiet Man is a 1952 John Wayne film, but here the two title words are separate pieces with the eating inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to cover it in its scabbard, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One who laments admitting beast of a drunken raver

indicators.note: the mourner lets the animal in

parts.note: someone who wails in grief is a wailer
an ass is a beast

explanation.surface: A mourner lets in some beast of a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beast of a drunken raver' reads as one phrase; split it so the animal is the insert and the raver the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassailer is a carouser who drinks healths, a reveller in drink.

clue.text: "Cheese without name" could be the solution

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the cheese surrounds the letter

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese

explanation.surface: A riddle claiming that an unnamed cheese is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking, so N goes inside BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is a solution of salt in water, used for pickling.

clue.text: Stop, say, arsing about with our daily leaders

indicators.note: the letters are messed about, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leading letters of the words our and daily

explanation.surface: Messing around with the daily paper's editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes O and D, and 'about' rearranges them with ARSING. 'leaders' suggests newspaper editorials.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop sign is one example of a roadside traffic notice, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Old computer fair's aircraft

parts.note: micro was the usual name for an early home microcomputer
fair hair is light hair

explanation.surface: An aircraft shown at an old computer fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like an exhibition but means pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A microlight is a very small, light powered aircraft.

clue.text: Musical abandon and glee

parts.note: to abandon is to desert
a glee is an unaccompanied part-song

explanation.surface: A show that abandons gaiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glee' reads as joy but is a kind of song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Song is a 1926 operetta by Sigmund Romberg, a stage musical.

clue.text: Separate the working horses, taking Kofi's side?

definitions.meaning: to unyoke a team of horses
Kofi Annan headed the United Nations

explanation.surface: Unharnessing horses while backing the UN Secretary-General.
explanation.definitionFit: To unteam is to unyoke a team of animals; read as UN plus team it is Annan's squad.

clue.text: Dim-looking stars unable to get "motivated" before end of scene

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes before the final letter
in quotes, the letters are set in motion, rearranged
the last letter of the word scene

explanation.surface: Faint stars cannot get going before a scene ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motivated' rearranges UNABLE to NEBULA; 'end of' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are faint cloudy patches in the sky, once taken for dim stars.

clue.text: Will follows hard on one masculine man in normal condition

indicators.note: the word for will comes after the three letters

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
I is the Roman numeral one
one's self in the sense of one's own will, as in self-will

explanation.surface: A will follows hard on a man being back to normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name or a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: To be oneself, for a man, is to be himself, in his usual state rather than unwell.

clue.text: Drink drunk before meal

indicators.note: the word for drunk goes in front

parts.note: high means intoxicated
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink taken drunk before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' says the word for intoxicated comes first, though it is printed second.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a British early-evening meal with tea and a cooked dish.

clue.text: Island folk getting over killer whale

indicators.note: in a down clue the people sit over the whale

parts.note: men as people, folk
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: Islanders recovering from a killer whale encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' looks like recovering but places MEN above ORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Menorca is one of Spain's Balearic Islands.

clue.text: Bar lost without the sound of a certain top dance

indicators.note: in the sense outside: the jumbled bar goes round the noise
the letters of bar are lost, scrambled

parts.words: the sound of a certain top
parts.note: a humming top makes a hum

explanation.surface: A bar is lost without some top dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' scrambles the bar into RBA, and 'without' wraps that round the noise. A humming top is a spinning toy that hums.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhumba, or rumba, is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: "Roll Over Beethoven", initially improvised with Erich

indicators.note: made up on the spot, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: only the first letter of the composer's name is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chuck Berry's Roll Over Beethoven, jammed with a man called Erich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll Over Beethoven' looks like the song title, but 'Roll' is the definition. 'improvised' rearranges O + B + ERICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, sweet French bread roll.

clue.text: Mendel, perhaps, was the first French writer here in French street

parts.note: Jean Genet was a French novelist and playwright
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: Gregor Mendel, a pioneer, here a French writer in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: Gregor Mendel founded the science of heredity, so he was the first of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendel's pea experiments made him the founding father of genetics.

clue.text: See 11
English poet's two conflicting responses

parts.note: the first answer is a refusal
the second answer is an assent

explanation.surface: A poet who cannot make up his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.

clue.text: Directed film about filling of Big Mac

indicators.note: the verb goes round the middle letter

parts.note: ran as in managed or directed

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word Big

parts.note: a film of paint is a coat

explanation.surface: Someone directed a film about what goes inside a Big Mac burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Mac' looks like the burger, but 'Mac' alone is the definition and 'filling of' takes only the middle letter of Big.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac is short for mackintosh, a waterproof outer garment.

clue.text: Depersonalised statue of god thus lacking height

indicators.note: the letter is missing from the joined pieces

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
so means thus

explanation.surface: A statue of a god, done like this but without its tall bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes H from THORSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is a statue of a body without head or limbs, so impersonal.

clue.text: How are you toppling Cherry without a pecking order?

parts.note: hi is a greeting like how are you

indicators.note: the scrambled fruit goes outside the letter
toppling knocks the letters over, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A greeting as a cherry tumbles, all orderly ranking gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppling' turns CHERRY into ERRCHY; 'without' puts it around A to give ERARCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecking order is a ranking by status, the same as a hierarchy.

clue.text: Gore found in retreating volcanic material's soft mixture

indicators.note: the name is placed inside the reversed rock
going back, the word is read backwards

parts.note: magma is molten volcanic rock
Al Gore, former US Vice President

explanation.surface: Al Gore turning up in lava as volcanic material cools to a mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the molten rock into AMGAM; 'found in' places the politician's first name inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a soft alloy of mercury, or any blend of things.

clue.text: Set steps taken by couples and armed soldiers

definitions.meaning: a quadrille danced by sets of couples

explanation.surface: Dance steps and troops on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: The lancers is a set dance for couples; lancers are also lance-carrying cavalry.
